constants.source: Derived: GGUF Q4_K super-block layout
constants.context: Q4_K block: 4 bytes (fp16 scale d + fp16 min m) + 12 bytes (8 sub-block scales + 8 minimums at 6 bits each, packed) + 128 bytes (256 four-bit codes) = 144 bytes for 256 weights, i.e. 4.5 bits/weight.

constants.source: Derived: 65,536 - 32,768 - 16 - 2 = 32,750; admission overhead 16 + 2
constants.context: Per-stream ceiling arithmetic: pool 65,536 positions minus reply budget 32,768 minus ROUND_ROWS 16 minus 2 guard positions leaves 32,750; the 18 positions beyond the reply budget are admission overhead.

constants.source: Derived: 12 x d_model^2 at d_model = 4,096
constants.context: A transformer layer with a 4d feedforward block performs about 12 x 4,096^2 = 201,326,592 ~ 201,300,000 multiply-adds in its linear projections, comparable to the head's d_model x V.

constants.source: Derived: e^10
constants.context: A ten-point logit gap becomes a probability ratio of e^10 ~ 22,026 to 1, because softmax exponentiates the score difference.
The logits head at V = 50,000 and d_model = 4,096 holds 204,800,000 parameters, about 205 million, removed entirely by weight tying.
KV traffic per rank falls from 120.5 MB at a 130,659-token prompt to 30.2 MB at the 32,750-token per-stream ceiling; the 90.3 MB difference at 273 GB/s is 0.33 ms per token.

constants.source: Derived: 4/(1+3f) = 1.80 solves to f = 0.407
constants.context: Under linear scaling the concurrency-4 speedup is 4/(1+3f) where f is the KV share of per-token traffic; setting it equal to the measured 1.80 gives f = 0.407, so KV traffic would have to be 40.7% of per-token traffic to explain the shortfall.

constants.source: Derived: 4/16 = 25%
constants.context: The decode round is pinned at 16 rows; at concurrency 4 only 4 rows are active, so the weight fetch is amortized 4x but the kernel's row slots are 25% utilized.

constants.source: Derived: 600 x 37.7 ms
constants.context: A long request with 600 tokens left at 37.7 ms per decode step needs 600 x 37.7 ms = 22.6 seconds of service.

constants.source: Measured on this machine (concurrency 1 decode step)
constants.context: Decode at concurrency 1 took 16.9 ms per step against 37.7 ms at concurrency 4, a 2.2x rise for 4x the tokens: the signature of a bandwidth-bound step amortizing a fixed weight fetch.

constants.source: Derived: 518,627 / 39,237 tokens per second
constants.context: The 518,627 uncached prompt tokens take 518,627 / 39,237 = 13.2 seconds of prefill compute; the cache removed the remaining 313 seconds.

constants.source: Derived: 512 / 39,237 tokens per second
constants.context: A 512-token prefill chunk costs 512 / 39,237 = 13.0 ms of compute, about a third of a 37.7 ms decode step at concurrency 4.

constants.source: Measured: tensorfold metrics, sampled window
constants.context: In the sampled window the engine counted 98 requests, 12,804,579 prompt tokens and 59,476 generated tokens, i.e. 130,659 prompt and 607 generated tokens per request.

constants.source: Derived: 4 tokens / 106.2 tok/s
constants.context: At concurrency 4 the engine sustains 106.2 tok/s across four streams, so each step emits four tokens and takes 4 / 106.2 = 37.7 ms; at concurrency 1 a step emits one token at 59.1 tok/s = 16.9 ms, a 2.2x rise for 4x the tokens.

constants.source: Derived: 106.2 tok/s / 4 streams
constants.context: At concurrency 4 a step emits four tokens in 37.7 ms, so each stream gets 106.2 / 4 = 26.5 tok/s while the aggregate nearly doubles; 106.2 / 59.1 = 1.80x.

constants.source: Derived: 12,804,579 prompt tokens - 12,285,952 cached tokens
constants.context: Over the sampled window 12,804,579 prompt tokens were looked up and 12,285,952 were cache hits (95.9%), leaving 518,627 uncached tokens that take 518,627 / 39,237 = 13.2 seconds of prefill.

constants.source: Derived: 175e9 params x 2 bytes (FP16)
constants.context: GPT-3 at 175 billion parameters needs 350 GB per token at FP16, so at 273 GB/s it could not exceed 0.78 tokens per second and would not fit.

constants.source: Derived: 989 TFLOP/s / 3.35 TB/s (NVIDIA H100 SXM datasheet)
constants.context: H100 SXM dense FP16 tensor throughput 989 TFLOP/s over HBM3 bandwidth 3.35 TB/s gives a ridge ratio near 295 FLOPs per byte, so a 130,000-token prefill is compute-bound while a decode step at intensity 1 is bandwidth-bound.

constants.source: Derived: 70e9 params x 2 bytes (FP16)
constants.context: A 70-billion-parameter model in FP16 occupies 140 GB, which no single device caches, so every decode step re-reads the weights.

constants.source: Derived: 0.676^2
constants.context: DSpark acceptance rate was 67.6% (42,181 accepted of 62,390 drafted); if drafts were independent the chance the second is accepted after the first is 0.676^2 = 45.7%, the third 30.9%, the fourth 20.9%.

constants.source: Derived: 70e9 params x 0.5 bytes (4-bit)
constants.context: A 70B model at 4 bits needs 35 GB, so 80 GB holds it only at 4 bits and holds nothing at FP16 (140 GB), giving a 273/35 = 7.8 tok/s ceiling.

constants.source: Derived: 1/s from the two-point fit (w+s=16.9, w+4s=37.7 => s=6.9 ms)
constants.context: Fitting step time as w + b*s to 16.9 ms at b=1 and 37.7 ms at b=4 gives s = 6.9 ms and w = 10.0 ms; the asymptote as b grows is 1/s = about 145 tokens per second, an upper bound because s itself grows with context.

constants.source: Derived: 100^2 x 64
constants.context: A dot product of two vectors with components near 100 over 64 dimensions can reach 100^2 x 64 = 640,000, which overflows fp16's largest finite value of 65,504.

constants.source: Derived: k x 2 x d_model x d_ff with k=2, d_model=4096, d_ff=14336
constants.context: Per token per MoE layer the selected experts cost k x 2 x d_model x d_ff = 2 x 2 x 4096 x 14336 = 234,881,024, about 235 million multiply-adds, against the router's d_model x E = 4096 x 64 = 262,144, roughly a tenth of a percent.

constants.source: Derived: 273 GB/s / 59.1 tok/s
constants.context: One stream at 59.1 tokens per second moves 273/59.1 = 4.62 GB of weights and cache per token; four concurrent streams at 106.2 aggregate give 273/106.2 = 2.57 GB per token, a 1.80 multiplier.

constants.source: Derived: 1.75 x 2^15 (e5m2 largest finite significand)
constants.context: For e5m2, bias 15 with exponent field 31 reserved for infinity and NaN gives a largest finite exponent of 15; the largest finite significand is 1.75, so 1.75 x 2^15 = 57,344.
Gradient scaling for the backward pass: a gradient tensor whose largest absolute value is 0.5 is scaled by 57,344 / 0.5 = 114,688 so its largest value becomes 57,344, the e5m2 maximum.

constants.source: NVIDIA Volta whitepaper (2017)
constants.context: The 2017 Volta whitepaper lists 125 TFLOPS fp16 tensor-core throughput against 15.7 TFLOPS fp32, roughly eight times the fp32 rate, which is why teams moved training to fp16.
If every byte of the 111.5 GB unified memory were weights it would be 27.9 billion parameters at fp32, 55.8 billion at bf16, or 111.5 billion at fp8; the fp8 figure is why fp8 matters.

constants.source: Derived: 3.33 s mean prefill x 98 requests
constants.context: Over the sampled window the mean prefill duration was 3.33 seconds over 98 requests, so total prefill time was 3.33 x 98 = 326.34 seconds.

constants.source: Derived: 518,627 uncached tokens / 326.34 s
constants.context: The actual computed prefill rate over uncached tokens was 518,627 / 326.34 = 1,589 tokens per second, against the apparent 12,804,579 / 326.34 = 39,237 tok/s that counts cached tokens as free work.

constants.source: Derived: 12,285,952 cached tokens / 1,589 tok/s
constants.context: Recomputing the 12,285,952 cached tokens at the computed 1,589 tok/s rate would cost 7,732 seconds, so a cold run takes 326.34 + 7,732 = 8,058 seconds and the cache removed 95.9 percent of cold prefill time.
A cold-cache prefill of the same 98 requests would take 326.34 + 7,732 = 8,058 seconds, roughly 25 times the warm run.

constants.source: Derived: 607 generated tokens / 8.38 s mean decode
constants.context: Mean decode duration over the 98 sampled requests is 8.38 seconds for 607 generated tokens, which is 607 / 8.38 = 72.4 tokens per second, against the 59.1 tok/s concurrency-one benchmark: both get called decode throughput.

If KV reads are small compared with the weight read the aggregate ceiling approaches 4 x 59.1 = 236.4 tok/s; the observed 106.2 is 45 percent of that, so the scheduler, batching or KV reads leave more than half the roofline unused.
